stories.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
stories.simple_summary: Meta changed the rules on its website to remove language that worried people about how the company collects information from the internet to train its AI system. The company says this change doesn't actually affect how they gather that information.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have a website, this might affect whether Meta can copy your content without paying you. Most small websites won't notice a change, but it's worth knowing what big tech companies can do with your work.

stories.title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic, an AI company, now has more experienced workers and spends more time in meetings than it did a year ago. This suggests the company is getting bigger and more formal.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people who work there. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Replit makes OpenAI its default over Anthropic, CEO says
stories.simple_summary: Replit, a website where programmers write code, switched to using OpenAI's AI assistant as the main choice instead of Anthropic's Claude. Users can still pick Claude if they want.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to programmers. If you're a small business owner who doesn't code, this won't affect you.

stories.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
stories.simple_summary: Meta removed specific text from its terms of service after people complained. The text suggested Meta could copy content from news websites and other sites to train AI. The language is now gone.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a news website or publish content online, you should know that companies are trying to use your work to train AI. Staying informed about these policies helps protect your business.

stories.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
stories.simple_summary: AI agents are computer programs that can do tasks on the internet by themselves, like booking restaurant reservations or buying things. However, many websites are now blocking these agents from entering.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a website or an online business, you may need to decide whether to allow these AI agents to visit. Right now it's a new issue, but it could become more important soon.

stories.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
stories.simple_summary: AI agents got into computer systems in India through passwords and settings that companies left exposed or didn't protect properly. This is a security problem.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use cloud services or store business information online, you need to make sure your passwords and settings are secure. Don't leave them where they can be easily found.

stories.title: An Nvidia insider-turned-VC on why robotics hasn’t hit its ChatGPT moment, yet
stories.simple_summary: An expert who worked at Nvidia says robotics is still in early stages, like building with basic Lego blocks. The pieces for real robots aren't finished yet, even though some people think we're close.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly technical discussion for investors. Robots that can do useful jobs aren't coming to small businesses any time soon.

stories.title: Physical AI is more than robots, says the Nvidia veteran now investing in it
stories.simple_summary: A former Nvidia leader is now investing in physical AI, which includes robots and other machines that interact with the real world, not just computers that answer questions.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and large companies. For small business owners, robot technology is still years away from being practical and affordable.

stories.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
stories.simple_summary: A company called Elorian made an AI model that can reason about images and charts instead of just describing what it sees. According to their tests, it performs better than a newer version of ChatGPT on certain tasks.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to engineers and investors. The average person won't notice a difference in their daily life.

stories.title: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
stories.simple_summary: Vercel, a platform for developers, released a new AI model called Jev that became very popular very quickly with its users.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to software developers. If you don't write code for a living, this won't affect your business.

stories.title: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia released a new powerful processor called RTX Spark for laptops that can compete with similar chips from Apple, Intel, and others. Reviewers have been testing computers with this new chip.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're thinking about buying a new laptop and want it to be fast and powerful, this is an option to consider. The specs are strong, though the price will likely be higher than budget laptops.

stories.title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
stories.simple_summary: Actor Mark Wahlberg says he's willing to use AI in movies to improve the filmmaking process and even allow an AI copy of himself to work after he retires.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to people in the film industry. For most businesses and individuals, this is just celebrity news and doesn't affect you directly.
